mechanism.owner_quote: A rolling deployment replaces instances in batches, so old and new versions serve traffic together during the rollout.
mechanism.reason: Defines batch replacement with old and new versions serving together.

invariant.owner_quote: Both versions must be compatible with the shared data and contracts for the whole overlap, or the rollout must stop before an incompatible state is written.
invariant.reason: Requires data and contract compatibility for the whole overlap.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Mixed versions expose an incompatibility that a single-version test missed; gate each batch on readiness and error signals and keep a tested stop condition.
failure_recovery.reason: Names mixed-version incompatibility and requires readiness/error gates and a stop condition.

alternative.owner_quote: Blue/green switches a complete environment at once; choose rolling when the extra capacity for a second environment is unavailable.
alternative.reason: Contrasts blue/green when a second environment is too costly.

mechanism.owner_quote: Blue/green runs two complete environments and switches traffic at a routing boundary, leaving the previous environment available for a short reversal.
mechanism.reason: Defines two environments and a routing switch with short reversal.

invariant.owner_quote: The switch must remain reversible until the new version's persisted effects are proven compatible with the old version.
invariant.reason: Requires reversibility until persisted effects are proven compatible.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A half-switched route or a new-only write makes reversal unsafe; verify routing completeness and data compatibility before declaring the cutover.
failure_recovery.reason: Names half-switched routes and new-only writes and requires routing/data checks.

alternative.owner_quote: A rolling or canary rollout uses less spare capacity; choose blue/green when a fast, complete reversal and a clean environment comparison justify the double capacity.
alternative.reason: Contrasts rolling/canary with lower spare capacity.

mechanism.owner_quote: Route a small, identifiable cohort to the new version and check that it is representative

invariant.owner_quote: The exposure slice is not a data-compatibility boundary

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Small samples hide rare errors, and an unrepresentative cohort can pass while a rare failure hides

alternative.owner_quote: Shadow traffic tests reads safely only when writes are suppressed; a mirrored write can execute twice.

mechanism.owner_quote: A runtime, versioned value scoped by tenant, user or cohort separates exposure from deployment, with a default and kill switch.

invariant.owner_quote: Flags never replace an authorization check.
invariant.reason: Explicit safety rule separating flags from authorization.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: on evaluation failure the default must be the safe branch, not a silent enable.

alternative.owner_quote: A canary or branch-by-abstraction is preferable when the toggle would become permanent configuration.

mechanism.owner_quote: GitOps treats a versioned desired-state repository as reviewed intent.

invariant.owner_quote: Rollback is a revert commit, which needs a linear, reviewable history and an immutable artifact reference.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Controller outage, drift, repository compromise and stale artifact references are common

alternative.owner_quote: A pipeline-driven deployment, manual release or imperative operator may be preferable when imperative one-off changes dominate or no reconciler owner exists.

mechanism.owner_quote: Immutable infrastructure replaces instances from a versioned image or definition instead of mutating running hosts, so each instance is reproducible from a recorded artifact.
mechanism.reason: Defines replacement from a versioned image or definition rather than mutation.

invariant.owner_quote: Every running instance must be reproducible from a recorded artifact digest, and drift must be detected rather than tolerated.
invariant.reason: Requires reproducibility from an artifact digest and drift detection.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A rebuilt image that no longer matches the deployed artifact turns replacement into an uncontrolled change; record digests and test the rebuild path.
failure_recovery.reason: Names rebuilt images that diverge and requires digest recording and rebuild tests.

alternative.owner_quote: choose immutable replacement when reproducibility, an automated replacement path and artifact rollback speed matter
alternative.reason: Names immutable replacement when reproducibility and fast artifact rollback matter.

mechanism.owner_quote: Intercept requests at a façade or route and send one capability at a time to the new implementation while the old path remains available.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: Keep one authoritative writer for each invariant and define routing plus data compatibility during coexistence.
invariant.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Interception may be impossible, internal callers may bypass the façade, and old/new state can diverge.
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: Branch by abstraction, parallel run or a big-bang replacement
alternative.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

mechanism.owner_quote: An internal interface can route old/new implementations with one deployable
mechanism.reason: Explains the internal abstraction that routes old and new implementations in one deployable.

invariant.owner_quote: Old and new implementations behind the internal interface must preserve the same contract and observable effects; the switch must remain reversible until the old path is removed.
invariant.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Untested side effects, a bypass around the abstraction and divergent implementations can break that contract.
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: A strangler facade can route requests by capability when the boundary is external.
alternative.reason: Names the strangler facade and its external-boundary condition.

mechanism.owner_quote: Expand-and-contract is a rollout protocol, not a schema diagram: each phase must remain compatible with readers still running the previous version, and the contract phase is gated by observed reader absence.
mechanism.reason: States the expand, migrate, verify and contract sequence.

invariant.owner_quote: New writers must preserve enough old representation for old supported readers until a verified cutover.
invariant.reason: States the compatibility precondition that must hold during coexistence.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Incompatible writes hold the rollout and may require forward repair rather than redeploying N.
failure_recovery.reason: Names the failure, the hold, and forward repair as recovery.

alternative.owner_quote: A big-bang migration, a parallel run or a versioned API cutover may be preferable when no mixed-version compatibility window is possible or the dataset is small enough to migrate under a verified pause.
